questions.question: What is the threshold amount for complaints to be auto-converted into an e‑Zero FIR?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹10 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** has implemented a mechanism where financial fraud complaints reported on the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCCRP)** involving an amount of **₹10 lakh** or more are automatically converted into an **e-Zero FIR**.
 
• This initiative is designed to ensure that **high-value financial frauds** are met with immediate legal action and formal investigation without the delay of jurisdictional disputes.
 
• The **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal** (www.cybercrime.gov.in) was launched in **2019** to allow victims to report all types of cybercrimes, especially those against women and children, and financial frauds.
 
• The **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, manages the portal and coordinates with **States and Union Territories** to handle these complaints.
 
• The auto-conversion into an **e-Zero FIR** helps in the rapid tracking of the **money trail** across multiple bank accounts and states, increasing the chances of recovering the defrauded amount. ***Hence, the correct answer is ₹10 lakh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero FIR:** 
 
 
• A **Zero FIR** is a First Information Report that can be filed in **any police station**, regardless of where the incident occurred.
 
• Unlike a regular FIR, it is given a **serial number '0'** (zero) and is later transferred to the police station that has the appropriate **jurisdiction** for investigation.
 
• This concept was introduced based on the recommendations of the **Justice Verma Committee** in **2013**, following the **Nirbhaya case**, to ensure that the police cannot refuse to register a complaint citing a lack of jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Cyber Fraud Helpline:**
 
 
• The **National Helpline Number 1930** (formerly 155260) is dedicated to reporting online financial frauds.
 
• It works in tandem with the **Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS)** to provide immediate assistance.
 
 
 
• **I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre):**
 
 
• Established in **2018**, it serves as a nodal point in the fight against **cybercrime** in India.
 
• It has several components including the **National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit** and the **National Cyber Crime Forensic Laboratory**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CFCFRMS System:** This system allows for the **real-time freezing** of funds. When a victim reports a fraud on **1930** or the portal, the **CFCFRMS** sends alerts to the respective **Banks** or **Wallets** to block the transaction before the fraudster can withdraw the money.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, which replaced the **CrPC**, has formalized the provisions for **Zero FIR** and **e-FIR**, making it mandatory for police stations to register them.
 
• **Data Fact:** Since its inception, the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal** has helped in saving **hundreds of crores** of rupees of citizens' money by facilitating the prompt blocking of defrauded amounts.
 
• The threshold of **₹10 lakh** was specifically chosen to prioritize **major scams** that involve significant economic loss and complex **inter-state** criminal networks.

questions.question: The Indian Prime Minister introduced a significant programme in the farming sector in October 2025 with a fund of ₹24,000 crore, named ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PM Dhan Dhaanya Krishi Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Prime Minister** announced the launch of a new flagship initiative for the **farming sector** in **October 2025**. This scheme is specifically designed to bolster agricultural infrastructure and output.
 
• The **PM Dhan Dhaanya Krishi Yojana** has been sanctioned with a significant financial outlay of **₹24,000 crore** to support farmers across the **country**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• This programme focuses on modernizing traditional farming practices and ensuring better market access for **rabi** and **kharif** crops, aiming to increase the **income** of small and marginal farmers.
 
• While **PM Fasal Bima Yojana** is an existing crop insurance scheme launched in **2016**, it does not match the specific funding and launch timeline mentioned in the question. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **PM Krishi Sinchai Yojana**, which focuses on **irrigation** ("Har Khet Ko Pani"), was formulated in **2015** and is distinct from the new **2025** initiative. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **PM Kisan Samman Yojana** (PM-KISAN) provides direct income support of **₹6,000** per year in **three installments** and was launched in **2019**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Budgetary Allocation for Agriculture:**
 
 
• The allocation of **₹24,000 crore** represents a substantial investment in the **Primary Sector** of the **Indian economy**.
 
• Large-scale funding of this nature is typically directed toward **technological integration**, such as **drones** for agriculture and **precision farming** tools.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN):**
 
 
• Launched on **February 24, 2019**, this central sector scheme provides **100% funding** from the **Government of India**.
 
• It targets **landholding farmer families** to supplement their financial needs for procuring various inputs.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY):**
 
 
• This scheme provides a comprehensive insurance solution against **natural calamities**, **pests**, and **diseases**.
 
• The **premium** rates are kept low for farmers: **2%** for **Kharif**, **1.5%** for **Rabi**, and **5%** for **commercial/horticultural** crops.
 
 
 
• **PM Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY):**
 
 
• Launched with the motto of **'More Crop Per Drop'**, it aims at improving **water-use efficiency** in the **farming sector**.
 
• It integrates multiple components like **Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme** (AIBP) and **Watershed Development**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **PM Dhan Dhaanya Krishi Yojana** is expected to address the challenges of **food security** and **crop diversification** in the upcoming **financial years**.
 
• The fund of **₹24,000 crore** is one of the highest dedicated outlays for a single agricultural scheme introduced in the **mid-2020s**.
 
• Implementation of such programs usually involves the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare** and state-level agricultural departments to ensure **last-mile delivery**.
 
• This initiative aligns with the national goal of **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) by reducing dependency on imported agricultural technologies and enhancing **domestic production** capacities.

questions.question: Who among the following was re-appointed as the Prime Minister of Portugal in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Luis Montenegro**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Luis Montenegro** is a prominent **Portuguese politician** who assumed the office of **Prime Minister** following the **legislative elections** held in **March 2024** and continued his leadership into **2025**. 
• He serves as the president of the **Social Democratic Party (PSD)**, which is the primary center-right political party in **Portugal**. 
• His appointment was formalized by **President Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa** after the **Democratic Alliance (AD)**, a center-right coalition led by **Montenegro**, secured the most seats in the national parliament. 
• **Luis Montenegro** succeeded **Antonio Costa**, who had served as the **Prime Minister** for eight years before resigning in **November 2023** due to a judicial probe. 
• The **Montenegro** administration's primary focus involves **economic liberalization**, **reducing income taxes**, and managing the **housing crisis** that has significantly affected **Portugal's** urban centers. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Democratic Alliance (AD):** 
• This political coalition was revived for the **2024 elections** and consists of the **PSD**, the **CDS – People's Party (CDS-PP)**, and the **Monarchist People's Party (PPM)**. 
• In the **230-seat Assembly of the Republic**, the **AD** won **80 seats**, requiring **Luis Montenegro** to lead a minority government. 
• **Antonio Costa:** 
• He was the **Prime Minister** of **Portugal** from **2015 to 2024** and a former leader of the **Socialist Party (PS)**. 
• His resignation followed **Operation Influencer**, an investigation into alleged corruption regarding **lithium** and **green hydrogen** projects. 
• **Pedro Nuno Santos:** 
• He is the current leader of the **Socialist Party (PS)**, having taken over after **Costa's** departure. 
• Under his leadership, the **PS** became the main opposition party after the **2024** electoral shift. 
• **Andre Ventura:** 
• He is the leader of the far-right party **Chega**, which saw a massive surge in popularity during the recent elections. 
• **Chega** quadrupled its parliamentary representation to **50 seats**, becoming the third-largest political force in **Portugal**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Portugal's Political System:** **Portugal** operates under a **semi-presidential system** where the **President** acts as the head of state and the **Prime Minister** as the head of government. 
• **Economic Landscape:** Under **Luis Montenegro**, the government has aimed for a **balanced budget** while attempting to spur growth through **private investment** and **structural reforms** in the **public health sector**. 
• **Date of Appointment:** **Luis Montenegro** was officially sworn in on **April 2, 2024**, and his cabinet survived a key confidence vote shortly thereafter, ensuring the stability of his premiership into **2025**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most polluted city in India as per the IQ Air Report 2024-25?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Byrnihat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Byrnihat**, a prominent industrial town located on the border of **Meghalaya** and **Assam**, has emerged as the most polluted city in **India** according to recent air quality data, including assessments aligned with the **IQAir** and **CREA** (Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air) reports for **2024**.
 
• The town has consistently recorded **PM2.5** levels that are drastically higher than the **World Health Organization (WHO)** safety limit, often exceeding **100 micrograms per cubic meter** on an annual average basis.
 
• The primary cause of severe air pollution in **Byrnihat** is the high concentration of **industrial units**, including **ferro-alloy plants**, **cement factories**, and **iron and steel mills** operating in the **EPIP (Export Promotion Industrial Park)** area.
 
• Geographically, **Byrnihat** is situated in a **valley-like terrain**, which leads to the phenomenon of **atmospheric inversion** during winter months, trapping toxic pollutants near the ground and preventing their dispersion.
 
• The **IQAir World Air Quality Report** and supplementary data for **2024-25** emphasize that while major metros like **Delhi** are frequently in the news, smaller industrial hubs like **Byrnihat** now face more critical **air quality index (AQI)** challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IQAir and Global Rankings**:
 
 
• **IQAir** is a **Swiss** air quality technology company that prepares the annual **World Air Quality Report** based on data from over **30,000** air quality monitoring stations worldwide.
 
• In the **2023** report (released in **2024**), **Begusarai** in **Bihar** was identified as the most polluted metropolitan area globally, but **Byrnihat** has topped specific national trackers for continuous pollution levels in **2024**.
 
 
 
• **PM2.5 and Health Impacts**:
 
 
• **PM2.5** refers to fine particulate matter with a diameter of less than **2.5 micrometers**, which can penetrate deep into the **lungs** and enter the **bloodstream**, causing **respiratory** and **cardiovascular** diseases.
 
• The **WHO** guideline for annual mean **PM2.5** concentration is **5 µg/m³**; however, most Indian cities exceed this by **10 to 20 times**.
 
 
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**:
 
 
• Launched by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** in **January 2019**, **NCAP** is a long-term, time-bound national strategy.
 
• It aims to achieve a **20% to 30%** reduction in particulate matter concentrations by **2024**, which was later updated to a goal of **40%** reduction by **2026** for **131 non-attainment cities**.
 
 
 
• **Pollution in Delhi and NCR**:
 
 
• **Delhi** and neighboring cities like **Gurugram** and **Faridabad** suffer from seasonal pollution peaks due to **stubble burning** in **Punjab** and **Haryana**, **vehicular emissions**, and **construction dust**.
 
• Despite being a major focus of policy interventions like the **GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan)**, **Delhi** remains one of the world's most polluted capital cities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monitoring Agencies**: Apart from **IQAir**, the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** in **India** monitors air quality through the **National Air Quality Index (AQI)**, which uses **eight pollutants** (PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb) to calculate the daily index.
 
• **Economic Impact**: Air pollution is estimated to cause a significant **GDP loss** to **India** due to health-related expenditures and lost **labor productivity**.
 
• **Industrial Regulation**: Cities like **Byrnihat** require stricter enforcement of **Green Tribunal (NGT)** norms to ensure that industrial emissions are scrubbed and filtered before release into the atmosphere.
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, Aman Sehrawat was honoured with the Arjuna Award; what sport does he compete in?

__

• In **January 2025**, he was conferred with the prestigious **Arjuna Award** by the **Government of India** in recognition of his extraordinary achievements in the field of **Wrestling**.
 
• He gained international fame by winning a **bronze medal** at the **2024 Paris Olympics**, making him **India's youngest-ever individual Olympic medalist** at the **age of 21**.
 
• He has been a consistent performer, securing a **gold medal** at the **2023 Asian Wrestling Championships** held in **Astana** and a **bronze medal** at the **2022 Hangzhou Asian Games**.
 
• Aman Sehrawat trains at the iconic **Chhatrasal Stadium** in **North Delhi**, which is famous for producing world-class wrestlers like **Sushil Kumar**, **Yogeshwar Dutt**, and **Ravi Kumar Dahiya**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Wrestling.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arjuna Award:** 
 
 
• Established in **1961**, it is **India's second-highest sporting honour**, presented by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• The award consists of a **statue of Arjuna**, a scroll, and a **cash prize of ₹15 lakh**.
 
• It is awarded to athletes who show good performance at the international level consistently for **four years** and display qualities of leadership and sportsmanship.
 
 
 
• **Other Distinguished Awards:**
 
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:** The **highest sporting honour** in India, previously known as the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.
 
• **Dronacharya Award:** This is presented to **coaches** for their excellence in sports coaching.
 
• **Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar:** Awarded to organizations and individuals who have played a visible role in the area of sports promotion and development.
 
 
 
• **Wrestling in India:** 
 
 
• **Wrestling** is one of the most successful individual sports for India at the **Olympic Games**, with medals won by **K.D. Jadhav** (**1952**), **Sushil Kumar** (**2008, 2012**), **Sakshi Malik** (**2016**), and **Bajrang Punia** (**2020**).
 
• The **Wrestling Federation of India (WFI)** is the governing body for the sport in the country.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other options:**
 
 
• **Weightlifting:** Notable Indian athletes include **Saikhom Mirabai Chanu** (Silver at **Tokyo 2020**).
 
• **Boxing:** Notable athletes include **Mary Kom** and **Lovlina Borgohain**.
 
• **Shooting:** Notable athletes include **Abhinav Bindra** and **Manu Bhaker** (Double bronze at **Paris 2024**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Aman Sehrawat's** rise is significant because he achieved **Olympic glory** shortly after losing both his parents at a young age, showcasing immense mental **resilience** and **discipline**.
 
• The **Arjuna Award** 2024-25 cycle highlights the government's focus on rewarding **young talent** who have brought laurels at the **Paris Olympics**.
 
• The selection committee for these awards is headed by a **retired judge** and includes former **Khel Ratna** and **Arjuna Awardees**.

questions.question: What is the name of the affordable insurance scheme launched by India Post Payments Bank (pilot launch was done in July 2023) for unorganised sector workers on 1 May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antyodaya Shramik Suraksha Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Antyodaya Shramik Suraksha Yojana** is an affordable **accident insurance scheme** specifically launched to provide a safety net for **unorganised sector workers**.
 
• The scheme is implemented through the **India Post Payments Bank (IPPB)** and the **Department of Posts**, leveraging their extensive reach to provide financial security to the **labour force**.
 
• A **pilot launch** of this insurance initiative was initially carried out in **July 2023** at **Nadiad** in the **Kheda district** of **Gujarat**, making it the first state in **India** to introduce such a scheme for **shramiks** (workers).
 
• Under this scheme, **unorganised workers** can receive insurance benefits of **Rs. 10 lakh** in the event of **accidental death** or **permanent disability**, helping their families manage financial crises.
 
• The **Antyodaya Shramik Suraksha Yojana** was formally extended on **1 May 2025** to further strengthen **social security** for workers who are often excluded from formal banking and insurance sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India Post Payments Bank (IPPB):**
 
 
• Established in **2018** under the **Department of Posts**, **Ministry of Communications**, with **100% equity** owned by the **Government of India**.
 
• Its primary objective is to drive **financial inclusion** by providing accessible banking services through over **1.55 lakh post offices** across the **country**.
 
 
 
• **Unorganised Sector and Welfare:**
 
 
• The **unorganised sector** in **India** comprises a vast majority of the workforce, including **construction workers**, **agricultural labourers**, and **street vendors**.
 
• The **e-Shram portal**, launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment**, serves as a comprehensive database to identify and assist these workers with **government schemes**.
 
 
 
• **Social Security Provisions:**
 
 
• Schemes like the **Antyodaya Shramik Suraksha Yojana** are part of the broader **social security** framework intended to meet **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)** related to poverty reduction.
 
• Other related schemes include the **Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM)**, which offers a **monthly pension** of **Rs. 3000** to workers after they reach the **age of 60**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The insurance coverage provided by **Antyodaya Shramik Suraksha Yojana** is highly competitive, often featuring **low annual premiums** starting around **Rs. 289** or **Rs. 499** depending on the specific policy tier chosen by the **beneficiary**.
 
• In case of the **death** of the insured worker, the **nominee** or family receives the **claim amount**, while in cases of **partial disability**, a significant portion of the sum assured is provided for **rehabilitation**.
 
• The collaboration between the **Post Office** and insurance companies ensures that workers in **rural areas** do not have to travel to urban centers to avail themselves of **insurance services**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the rank of India in the Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2025, published by the Hurun Research Institute, which marks a significant milestone in the global startup ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** has secured the **3rd** position globally in the **Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2025**, published by the **Hurun Research Institute**.
 
• This ranking signifies that **India** continues to maintain its status as one of the world's premier startup ecosystems, trailing only behind the **United States** and **China**.
 
• The index defines a **unicorn** as a startup founded in the **2000s** that has a valuation of at least **$1 billion** and is not yet listed on a public exchange.
 
• According to the **2025** report, **India** possesses a total of **67** unicorns, showcasing a robust entrepreneurial environment despite global economic fluctuations.
 
• The **United States** leads the global tally with **703** unicorns, while **China** holds the second spot with **340** unicorns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Unicorns:**
 
 
• The term **"Unicorn"** was first coined by venture capitalist **Aileen Lee** in **2013** to describe rare private startups valued at over **$1 billion**.
 
• In addition to unicorns, the **Hurun Research Institute** tracks **"Decacorns"** (startups valued over **$10 billion**) and **"Hectocorns"** (startups valued over **$100 billion**).
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distribution in India:**
 
 
• **Bengaluru** remains the **"Unicorn Capital of India"**, hosting the highest density of billion-dollar startups in the country.
 
• Other significant hubs include **Mumbai**, **Gurugram**, and **Noida**, which contribute significantly to the **National Startup Ecosystem**.
 
 
 
• **Prominent Sectors:**

__
 
• **Civil Services Day** is celebrated every year on **April 21** in India to recognize the contribution of officers engaged in various public service departments.
 
• The theme for the **17th Civil Services Day** was **Holistic Development of India**, focusing on the integration of various government schemes to ensure comprehensive progress across the nation. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The date **April 21** was chosen to commemorate the day in **1947** when **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, the first **Home Minister** of independent India, addressed the probationers of **Administrative Service Officers**.
 
• In his historic speech at **Metcalf House** in **Delhi**, **Sardar Patel** referred to civil servants as the **"Steel Frame of India"**, highlighting their pivotal role in maintaining the country's administration and integrity.
 
• The celebration serves as an occasion for civil servants to rededicate themselves to the cause of the citizens and renew their commitment to public service and excellence in work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Institutional Framework:**

• They are responsible for the implementation of **government policies** and the delivery of **essential services** to the public at the **grassroots level**.

questions.question: India has banned jute imports from which country through all land and sea ports except Nhava Sheva in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the Government of India, through the **Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)**, implemented a major policy shift by restricting the import of jute and jute products from **Bangladesh**.
 
• The notification specifies that these imports are now prohibited through all land and sea ports across the country, with the sole exception of the **Nhava Sheva** port (Jawaharlal Nehru Port) located in **Maharashtra**.
 
• This move is aimed at strictly monitoring the quality of imported jute and ensuring that **anti-dumping regulations** are effectively enforced to protect domestic manufacturers. ***Hence, the option Bangladesh is correct.***
 
• Prior to this, a significant volume of jute entered India through land border crossings in **West Bengal**, such as **Petrapole**, but the new mandate redirects all traffic to a single maritime gateway for better oversight.
 
• The restriction is expected to impact the supply chain of the Indian **jute industry**, which relies on high-quality fiber from **Bangladesh** to supplement domestic production.
 
• Other neighboring countries like **Pakistan**, **Nepal**, and **China** do not have similar port-specific restrictions for jute in this specific **June 2025** directive. ***Hence, these options are incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Bangladesh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Golden Fiber:** **Jute** is known as the "Golden Fiber" due to its shiny golden color and high economic value. It is a **biodegradable** and **eco-friendly** natural fiber, primarily used for making gunny bags, twine, and carpets.
 
• **Jute Production in India:** India is the **world's largest producer** of raw jute. The state of **West Bengal** accounts for over **70%** of the country's total production, followed by Bihar and Assam.
 
• **Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987:** This **Act** makes the use of jute packaging mandatory for certain commodities. For example, **100% of food grains** and **20% of sugar** must be packed in diversified jute bags to support the livelihood of **4 million farmers** and hundreds of thousands of mill workers.
 
• **Jute Corporation of India (JCI):** Established in **1971**, the **JCI** is the nodal agency of the Government of India for the purchase of raw jute from farmers at the **Minimum Support Price (MSP)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nhava Sheva Port:** Also known as **Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT)**, it is the largest container port in India. Its selection as the exclusive entry point allows for centralized **customs clearance** and rigorous **quality testing** by specialized agencies.
 
• **Trade Dynamics with Bangladesh:** **Bangladesh** is the second-largest producer of jute globally. India often imports specific grades of jute fiber from **Bangladesh** that are used for blending or high-end exports.
 
• **Anti-Dumping Duty:** India has previously imposed **anti-dumping duties** on jute goods originating from **Bangladesh** and **Nepal** to prevent the domestic market from being flooded with cheap imports that could harm local **jute mills**.
 
• **Climatic Requirements:** Jute cultivation requires a **warm and humid climate** with temperatures between **24°C and 38°C** and annual rainfall of more than **150 cm**. It grows best in **alluvial soil** found in the **Ganges-Brahmaputra delta**.

questions.question: The Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme launched in 2025 is part of which key national programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Green Hydrogen Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme**, officially detailed in **2024-2025**, is a critical regulatory framework under the **National Green Hydrogen Mission** to verify and certify the carbon intensity of hydrogen produced in **India**.
 
• The **National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM)** was approved by the **Union Cabinet** on **4 January 2023**, with an initial financial outlay of **₹19,744 crore** to transition the economy to a low-carbon path.
 
• This certification scheme ensures that hydrogen production meets the specific "Green" standards, which require that carbon emissions do not exceed **2 kg CO2 equivalent per kg of hydrogen** produced.
 
• It serves as a mechanism to facilitate **international trade**, allowing Indian producers to demonstrate compliance with global environmental standards, such as those required by the **European Union** and other **Global North** markets.
 
• The scheme is overseen by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**, which acts as the nodal ministry for implementing the mission's objectives and coordinating with the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Green Hydrogen Mission Targets**:
 
 
• The mission aims to develop a green hydrogen production capacity of at least **5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT)** per annum by the year **2030**.
 
• It seeks to add about **125 Gigawatts (GW)** of renewable energy capacity to the country's grid specifically for hydrogen production.
 
• The mission is expected to reduce **fossil fuel imports** by over **₹1 lakh crore** and abate nearly **50 MMT** of annual greenhouse gas emissions by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Green India Initiative**:
 
 
• This is part of the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**, primarily focused on **afforestation**, protecting **biodiversity**, and increasing **forest cover** across **India**.
 
 
 
• **National Solar Energy Mission**:
 
 
• Launched in **January 2010**, it is a major initiative to promote **solar power** and establish **India** as a global leader in solar energy by creating policy conditions for its diffusion across the country.
 
 
 
• **SIGHT Programme**:
 
 
• The **Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT)** is a financial incentive mechanism under the mission that provides **subsidies** for **electrolyzer manufacturing** and **green hydrogen production**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Decarbonization of Hard-to-Abate Sectors**: The certification scheme is vital for industries like **Steel**, **Refineries**, and **Fertilizers**, which are the primary consumers of hydrogen and need verified green sources to reach **Net Zero** targets.
 
• **Well-to-Gate Scope**: The certification follows a **well-to-gate** boundary, encompassing water treatment, electrolysis, gas purification, drying, and compression of hydrogen.
 
• **Nodal Agencies**: While **MNRE** is the lead, the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)** is the designated agency for the **accreditation** of agencies that will carry out the actual **monitoring, verification, and certification** of projects.
 
• **Environmental Commitment**: This initiative aligns with **India’s** commitment at **COP26** to achieve **Net Zero emissions** by the year **2070**.

b1:T

questions.question: Which of the following was inducted in the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves in September 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve**, located in the state of **Himachal Pradesh**, was inducted into the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR)** in **September 2025**.
 
• This reserve spans across the **Spiti Valley** and includes significant protected areas such as the **Pin Valley National Park**, **Chandertal**, and **Sarchu**.
 
• It is characterized by its high-altitude **trans-Himalayan** ecosystem, featuring extreme cold temperatures and arid conditions, which support a unique variety of flora and fauna.
 
• The reserve is a critical habitat for endangered species, most notably the **Snow Leopard** (Panthera uncia), and serves as a vital zone for conservation and scientific research under **UNESCO's** international standards.
 
• The inclusion of the **Cold Desert** in the **WNBR** aims to promote sustainable development while ensuring the protection of the delicate ecological balance of the **Himalayan** region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR):**
 
 
• The **WNBR** is an international network created by **UNESCO** under the **Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme** launched in **1971**.
 
• It seeks to establish a scientific basis for the improvement of relationships between people and their environments, promoting the **conservation of biodiversity** and **sustainable use** of resources.
 
 
 
• **Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, it was designated as a Biosphere Reserve by the **Government of India** in **1999** and added to the **UNESCO WNBR** in **2009**.
 
• It includes **Satpura National Park** and serves as a transition zone between the **Deccan Plateau** and the **Gangetic Plains**.
 
 
 
• **Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• This reserve covers parts of **Chhattisgarh** and **Madhya Pradesh**. It was included in the **UNESCO** list in **2012**.
 
• It is known for being the source of the **Narmada**, **Johilla**, and **Son Rivers** and features diverse topography from hills to plains.
 
 
 
• **Kachchh Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• Situated in **Gujarat**, it is the largest Biosphere Reserve in **India** by area.
 
• It is famous for the **Great Rann of Kutch** and provides a sanctuary for the **Indian Wild Ass** (Khur) and several migratory birds like **Flamingos**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• India currently has **18** designated **Biosphere Reserves**, with many of them now recognized under the **UNESCO World Network**.
 
• The first Biosphere Reserve to be established in **India** was the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** in **1986**, which was also the first to join the **UNESCO** list in **2000**.
 
• **Biosphere Reserves** are divided into three zones: the **Core Area** (strictly protected), the **Buffer Zone** (used for research and education), and the **Transition Area** (where sustainable human activities occur).
 
• The designation of these sites helps in implementing the **Convention on Biological Diversity** and the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** set by the **United Nations**.
</ul

questions.question: Which award did President Murmu present to the Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**E-Governance Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The President of India, **Smt. Droupadi Murmu**, presented the **National Award for e-Governance 2024-25** to the **Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM)** in **January 2025**.
 
• The award was conferred in recognition of the **Indian Bureau of Mines'** exemplary implementation of digital solutions to enhance transparency, accountability, and efficiency in the mining sector.
 
• Specifically, the recognition was for the **Mining Surveillance System (MSS)** and the **Integrated Mines and Minerals Management System**, which utilize **satellite imagery** and **remote sensing technology** to monitor mining activities across the country.
 
• The **e-Governance Award** highlights the shift towards a "Digital India" where **Information and Communication Technology (ICT)** is used to curb illegal mining and ensure the sustainable development of mineral resources. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• The evaluation for this award is conducted by the **Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)** under the **Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM):**
 
 
• Established on **1st March 1948**, it is a multi-disciplinary government organization under the **Ministry of Mines**.
 
• The **Headquarters** of the **Indian Bureau of Mines** is located in **Nagpur, Maharashtra**.
 
• Its primary function is the **conservation of minerals**, protection of the environment in mines, and the scientific development of mineral resources (excluding coal, petroleum, and natural gas).
 
 
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award:**
 
 
• It is a **literary honor** in India, established in **1954**.
 
• The award is presented annually by the **Sahitya Akademi** to writers of the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the **24 major Indian languages** (including English and Rajasthani). ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **National Sports Awards:**
 
 
• These are a collection of honors awarded by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** to sportspersons for their achievements.
 
• Major categories include the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**, the **Arjuna Award**, and the **Dronacharya Award**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna:**
 
 
• Instituted in **1954**, it is the **highest civilian award** of the Republic of India.
 
• It is awarded in recognition of exceptional service or performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor, without distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mining Surveillance System (MSS):**
 
 
• This is a **satellite-based monitoring system** developed by the **Ministry of Mines** in collaboration with **Bhaskaracharya Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N)**.
 
• It aims to establish a regime of responsive mineral administration by using **space technology** to detect unauthorized mining activities within **500 meters** of lease boundaries.
 
• The system triggers "triggers" or alerts when land-use changes are detected, which are then verified by field officials using a **mobile app**.
 
 
 
• **National e-Governance Awards:**
 
 
• These awards recognize and promote excellence in the implementation of **e-Governance initiatives** by various government departments and startups.
 
• The awards are usually divided into categories such as **Gold** and **Silver**, providing financial incentives and certificates to the winning teams.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is the estimated fiscal deficit for the financial year 2025–26 as per Union Budget, 2025–26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.4% of GDP**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025–26** was presented in the **Parliament** of India by the **Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman** on **February 1, 2025**.
 
• For the financial year **2025-26**, the **Fiscal Deficit** is estimated to be **4.4% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**. This target is a significant milestone in the government's **fiscal consolidation** roadmap.
 
• This estimate follows the **Revised Estimate (RE)** of the previous financial year (2024-25), where the fiscal deficit was pegged at **4.9%**. The reduction to **4.4%** demonstrates a disciplined approach to managing the **national debt**.
 
• The government had previously set a target in the **2021-22 Budget** to reach a fiscal deficit level below **4.5% of GDP** by the year **2025-26**. By setting the target at **4.4%**, the government has successfully stayed ahead of its projected trajectory.
 
• The fiscal deficit represents the difference between the **Total Expenditure** of the government and its **Total Receipts** (excluding borrowings). A deficit of **4.4%** indicates the extent to which the government must borrow to fund its operations and investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Fiscal Deficit:**
 
 
• It is a key indicator of the **financial health** of the economy. It shows the total **borrowing requirements** of the government from all sources, including **Market Borrowings** and the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
• A lower fiscal deficit generally leads to lower **inflation** and lower interest rates, which encourages **private investment**.
 
 
 
• **Capital Expenditure (Capex):**
 
 
• Despite fiscal tightening, the **Union Budget 2025-26** continues to prioritize **Capital Expenditure** to boost **infrastructure development**, such as **Railways**, **Highways**, and **Renewable Energy** projects.
 
• The **multiplier effect** of Capex is essential for sustaining long-term **Economic Growth** and job creation.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts:**
 
 
• The fiscal target is supported by strong growth in **Tax Revenue**, including **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, **Corporate Tax**, and **Personal Income Tax**.
 
• Non-tax receipts, such as **dividends** from the **RBI** and **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**, also play a vital role in meeting the deficit targets.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **FRBM Act:** The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003**, provides the legal framework for reducing the fiscal deficit and ensuring **inter-generational equity** in fiscal management.
 
• **Financing the Deficit:** In **2025-26**, the gross and net **market borrowings** are managed to ensure there is enough **liquidity** available for the private sector, preventing the **crowding out** effect.
 
• **Global Context:** India's commitment to a **4.4%** fiscal deficit is viewed positively by **Global Rating Agencies**, which helps maintain India's **investment-grade** sovereign rating.
 
• **Nominal GDP Growth:** The fiscal deficit percentage is calculated based on the estimated **Nominal GDP** growth for the **year 2025-26**, which accounts for both real growth and **inflation**.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes was launched by the Gujarat government in May 2025 that sends real-time SMS alerts to citizens about their police case progress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I-Pragati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of Gujarat** launched the **I-Pragati** scheme in **May 2025** to revolutionize citizen-police interactions through technology.
 
• The **I-Pragati** system is designed to provide **real-time SMS alerts** to complainants regarding the status and progress of their police cases, ensuring they stay informed without manual follow-ups.
 
• Under this scheme, citizens receive automated notifications for various stages of the legal process, including the **registration of an FIR**, the **appointment of an Investigating Officer (IO)**, and the **submission of the charge sheet** or final report in court. ***Hence, the option I-Pragati is correct.***
 
• The initiative aims to enhance **transparency**, **accountability**, and **public trust** by bridging the communication gap between the **Gujarat Police** and the general public.
 
• By utilizing the **CCTNS (Crime and Criminal Tracking Network & Systems)** database, the system automatically triggers messages to the registered **mobile number** of the victim or complainant as soon as an update is entered into the police records.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **e-FIR Service in Gujarat:**
 
 
• Prior to **I-Pragati**, **Gujarat** had already established a robust digital framework, including an **e-FIR** portal for reporting **mobile phone** and **vehicle thefts** online.
 
• This service allows citizens to file complaints for specific non-heinous crimes through a **web portal** or **mobile application**, reducing the footfall at physical **police stations**.
 
 
 
• **CCTNS Project:**
 
 
• The **Crime and Criminal Tracking Network & Systems (CCTNS)** is a **National e-Governance** initiative aimed at creating a nationwide integrated system for sharing **real-time crime data** across different states.
 
• In **Gujarat**, the high level of **CCTNS implementation** has enabled the integration of various citizen-centric services like **I-Pragati**.
 
 
 
• **VISWAS Project:**
 
 
• The **Video Integration and State Wide Advanced Security (VISWAS)** is another major project by the **Gujarat Government**.
 
• It involves the installation of over **7,000 CCTV cameras** across **33 districts** for traffic management, crime prevention, and detection.
 
 
 
• **Digital India and Gujarat:**
 
 
• **Gujarat** consistently ranks high in **e-governance** indices in **India**, implementing various digital solutions like the **Pocket Cop** project, which provides **smartphones** to police officers for instant verification of **criminal records** and **passport verifications**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Real-time Updates:**
 
 
• The introduction of **SMS alerts** helps in curbing **corruption** and **delays** by making the police process more visible to the public.
 
• It specifically benefits individuals in **rural areas** who previously had to travel long distances to **district headquarters** or **police stations** just to inquire about their case status.
 
• The **I-Pragati** scheme reflects the **"Minimum Government, Maximum Governance"** philosophy by automating administrative communications.
